subject: Isolated-net deployment readiness questionnaire & staffing ask
messages:
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Oct 2028 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Isolated-net deployment request from Asteron — ask for architecture + staffing inputs

Team —

Asteron Health (contact: Dana Li) engaged us this morning about a privately hosted deployment in their VPC / on-prem colocation. They shared a short requirements doc (attached) and asked for a feasibility note + an initial staffing estimate by EOD tomorrow so they can include it in their procurement packet. High level items they care about:

- Physically isolated deployment (no public ingress except through customer-managed bastion)
- HSM/KMS for key material (customer-managed preferred)
- Quarterly audit logs retention and controlled access (audit-friendly backups)
- SLA: 99.9% for inference API, with burst handling during business hours
- Expected 5-10 tpm (total prompt/min is low but unpredictable spikes during business demos)

Can you each take the relevant pieces and reply with:
1) Karthik: a short bullet list of architecture gaps / unknowns and any software changes we'd need in runtime to support their isolation profile (e.g., no outbound telemetry, custom KMS plugin).
2) Hannah: high-level headcount + oncall overhead (Dev, Ops, Security), and any hiring/contractor assumptions in the estimate.
3) Kimberly: compliance evidence we can offer initially (SOC2 artifacts, minimal audit package) and any lead time for additional reports.

I attached their requirements and a rough sketch I sketched in a call. I will coordinate a short 30-min sync with Dana once we have internal notes — ideally tomorrow morning PT.

Thanks — appreciate concise bullets.

--
Rafael Mendes
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
rafael_mendes@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0143

Attachments: customer-requirements-asteron.docx, arch-draft-v1.pdf
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Oct 2028 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Isolated-net deployment request from Asteron — initial architecture notes

Rafael —

Thanks for the heads up. Quick initial thoughts (more detail in JIRA INFRA-9273):

- Network: customer's request for no public egress from hosts means we need to support a private-only runtime. That will require us to:
  * Build a no-telemetry runtime mode (opt-out at process level) — currently we have telemetry toggles but not a fully air-gapped mode.
  * Support customer-supplied NAT/bastion proxies for outbound code/patch pulls and for WebSocket tunneling for management.

- Key management:
  * KMS integration: we can add a KMS plug-in; code-level surface exists but we'll need a sprint to harden key rotation and envelope encryption.
  * HSM: if they require HSM-backed signing operations in the runtime, we need hardware bindings and vendor testing (approx 4–6 weeks of validation).

- Storage & logs:
  * Audit log retention can be configured to push to customer S3 equivalent — we need to ensure our log format and access controls match the customer's compliance policy.
  * Backups of model weights: if customer requires on-prem copies, validate licensing for any third-party models.

- Runtime changes:
  * Disable outbound metrics ingestion by default, add dry-run to simulate metrics locally.
  * KV cache persistence policy: ensure that cache doesn't leak across tenants — quick audit needed.

Open questions for Dana I want answered before we size work:
1) Do they require zero outbound connections at all times, or is management plane allowed for patching (schedule-based)?
2) Which KMS/HSM vendors do they expect to use?
3) Acceptance criteria for audit logs (format, retention length, who signs off)?

I attached a short architecture sketch (arch-draft-v1.pdf) and created INFRA-9273 for tracking. If we get a yes/know on the management plane, I can carve a minimal engineering plan (2 sprints) vs. full air-gap (6–8 weeks).

-Karthik

Attachments: arch-draft-v1.pdf
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Oct 2028 18:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Isolated-net deployment request from Asteron — staffing estimate

Rafael / Karthik —

High-level staffing view (ballpark for an initial pilot):

- Delivery sprint (feature work to reach minimal viable private runtime): 8 weeks
  * 2x Senior Backend Engineers (runtime / security) — full time for 8 weeks
  * 1x DevOps Engineer (private networking, deployment templates) — 50% for 8 weeks
  * 1x Security Engineer (integration, HSM/KMS validation) — 25% for 8 weeks

- Ongoing run (per-customer overhead):
  * 0.25 FTE Production Engineer (monitoring, deployments)
  * 0.10 FTE Security (audit liaising)
  * Oncall: +1 escalation rotation from production team; we estimate one extra incident response rotation per quarter per pilot (additional pager cost).

Assumptions / caveats:
- This assumes we can reuse our existing model-serving images and only add configuration branches for no-telemetry and KMS plugin. If we need a separate build flavor or HSM-specific binaries, add one senior engineer (4-6 weeks).
- If the customer requires 24/7 standby support with SLA-backed response windows, we need formal enterprise support headcount and an SRE contract.

I attached an update to the headcount sheet (headcount_estimate_v2.xlsx). We should also confirm whether procurement expects this to be capitalized or billed as professional services.

-Hannah

Date: Thu, 26 Oct 2028 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Isolated-net deployment request from Asteron — next steps + questions

Dana —

Thanks for the quick call earlier. Internal team has pulled together an initial list of open items (below) so we can size and give a clean estimate to your procurement team:

Open items we need confirmation on:
1) Management plane policy: do you permit scheduled outbound connections for patching and telemetry, or is it strictly no outbound at all times?
2) KMS/HSM vendor preference (we support AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault, Vault PKCS#11 integrations; HSM vendor compatibility will affect validation time).
3) Audit log spec: retention window and whether logs can be pushed to a customer S3/GCS bucket (format JSONL preferred).
4) SLA expectations for pilot (target API p99 latency; escalation windows).

Internal asks for Asteron procurement:
- We propose a pilot SOW covering 8 weeks of engineering + 3 months of operational support for validation. Headcount and estimate will be shared after you confirm items above.
- Please share any mandatory vendor paperwork (e.g., required clauses for on-prem deployment) and the procurement timeline.

Proposed next step: short 30-min sync tomorrow 10:00 AM PT to go through those four items. Please accept the calendar invite I sent.

Best,
Rafael

Onward —
Rafael Mendes
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
rafael_mendes@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Isolated-net deployment request from Asteron — next steps + questions

Rafael / team —

Thanks for the clear summary. Quick answers:

1) Management plane: we prefer management plane to be restricted to scheduled windows (weekly patch window and emergency window with explicit approval). Zero permanent outbound allowed.
2) KMS/HSM: primary preference is Thales HSM, but we can use Vault PKCS#11 adapter if that reduces validation time.
3) Audit logs: 7 years retention; pushing to our secure S3 endpoint is fine. JSONL preferred.
4) SLA: for the pilot we can accept SLOs (best-effort), procurement will push for 99.9% in production.

I uploaded our vendor checklist and the procurement timeline to the drive link you shared and accepted the 10:00 AM PT slot. I also shared a DocuSign template for preliminary SOW review: https://docusign.com/tx/AST-PO-001

Looking forward to the sync.

Best,
Dana Li

Asteron Health
